stories.title: Baseball Hall of Fame Induction Weekend — Beltran and Andruw Jones Tomorrow
stories.angle: Carlos Beltran and Andruw Jones will be inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame at the induction ceremony Sunday, July 26, in Cooperstown, New York. Beltran: .279/.350/.490 career slash line, 435 home runs, 2,725 hits, 312 stolen bases, 9 Gold Gloves, 9-time All-Star, switch-hitter widely regarded as one of the best offensive players of his generation. Jones: .254/.330/.486, 434 HR, 10 consecutive Gold Gloves in center field (1998-2007), regarded by analytics as one of the greatest defensive players in baseball history. Beltran's candidacy carried the context of his involvement in the 2017 Astros sign-stealing investigation; the BBWAA ultimately decided his playing career merited enshrinement.

stories.title: Ohtani Pitching Timeline — Roberts Says No Return Date
stories.angle: Dodgers manager Dave Roberts confirmed Saturday that Shohei Ohtani will not make his next scheduled pitching start and there is no timetable for his return to the mound. Ohtani has been dealing with left knee irritation that may relate to a 2019 surgery. He has not pitched since July 3, when he was 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 95 strikeouts in 85.2 innings — on pace for a potential Cy Young Award. He threw approximately 31 pitches in a bullpen session July 22. The Dodgers expect him to pitch again in 2026, but Roberts would not give a timeline. He continues to DH and hit.

stories.title: Phillies Pitching Records — Sanchez Breaks 115-Year Franchise Mark
stories.angle: Two significant Phillies records fell this week. Cristopher Sanchez extended his scoreless innings streak to 41⅔ innings, breaking a 115-year-old Phillies franchise record held by Grover Cleveland Alexander. Kyle Schwarber hit his 30th home run, reaching that mark in the fewest team games in Phillies franchise history. Sanchez's streak is a masterclass in contact management and pitch sequencing. Together, these performances underscore why Philadelphia has one of the strongest pitching situations in the National League heading into the August 3 trade deadline.

stories.title: MLB Trade Deadline — Nine Days Away and Heating Up
stories.angle: The MLB Trade Deadline is August 3 at 6 PM ET — nine days away. The market is accelerating. Key names: Mason Miller (Padres closer, under team control through 2029, 2026 All-Star — Yankees "love the idea" of acquiring him). Tarik Skubal (Tigers ace, trade odds reported at 60% by ESPN's Jeff Passan). Angels in fire-sale mode — Jose Soriano, Reid Detmers, and Zach Neto all available. Tampa Bay Rays expected to be major buyers. Mets moving into full sell mode. Phillies have become "more willing to discuss higher-caliber arms." The next nine days will reshape October contenders.

stories.title: The Milestones Notebook — Ramirez 30/30, Freeman 400/2500, Misiorowski 105.5 mph
stories.angle: July 2026 has been a week for the record books across multiple teams. Jose Ramirez (Guardians) is on pace to become only the second player in history — after Barry Bonds — to hit 30 HR and steal 30 bases in three consecutive seasons. Freddie Freeman (Dodgers) is tracking toward 400 career HR and 2,500 career hits — only the 18th player ever to reach both thresholds. Jacob Misiorowski (Brewers) registered a 105.5 mph pitch — the fastest pitch ever recorded from a starting pitcher under modern tracking technology, tying Ben Joyce for third-fastest pitch all-time. Aroldis Chapman also set the career strikeout record for relief pitchers earlier this month, surpassing Hoyt Wilhelm with strikeout No. 1,364.
